## Epic X6: Claims Register

*One file that maps every public assertion to its evidence, and a gate that keeps it honest.*

| Story | Size | Status | Summary |
|-------|------|--------|---------|
| X6.1 | M | **Done** | **Create `docs/claims.md`** — Every externally-visible claim in `README.md`, `docs/features-loke.md`, `docs/features-moke.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the public site, with a verdict (verified / partial / stub / absent), the implementing code at file and line, and the test or measurement that proves it. Seed it from the audit already completed. |
| X6.2 | S | **Done** | **Mark unverified claims inline** — Apply an explicit marker to every claim in the register that is not verified, so the assertion stays visible but flagged, using the withdrawal idiom already established on the public site rather than inventing a new one. |
| X6.3 | S | **Done** | **CI gate** — Fail the build when a claim marked verified has no evidence pointer, and when a published figure has no corresponding entry in `docs/metrics-baseline.md`. `scripts/check_claims.py` implements both checks (standard library only, `--check` mode for CI) and runs in CI through `scripts/quality-gate.sh --step checks`, which the `static-checks` job invokes — so the gate is live and needs no compiler. It is called from the gate script rather than named directly in the workflow, which is why a grep of `.github/` finds nothing. |
| X6.4 | S | **Done** | **Correct the coverage statement** — `docs/test-coverage.md` reports 35.5% module coverage, which counts files that have a test rather than modules actually exercised; of 86 test files, 54 carry an explicit stub marker and re-declare the module under test instead of importing it, and only about 12 import real production code. State both numbers and what each means. |
| X6.5 | S | **Done** | **Withdraw unsupported results language** — `docs/research/research-proposal.md:15` states "We present empirical benchmarks demonstrating" token savings, detection accuracy and call reduction figures that no measurement produced. Rewrite as proposed methodology pending execution. |

## Epic X8: Security Guarantee Hardening

*The controls that documents describe as protections and that do not operate. Cited in thirteen files
before this epic existed, which is why it is written now.*

> **Unblocked 2026-09-20.** `std.encrypt` is a toke library and the toolchain is available, so this epic
> is live. X8.5 stays held behind NC1.9 because `pipeline.tk` must not be edited until the fail-open is
> fixed. The stories still queue behind a compiling build — see F10.

| Story | Size | Status | Summary |
|-------|------|--------|---------|
| X8.1 | S | **Done** — 2026-09-23 | **Reverse the GA2.2 marking, and delete the false control rather than repair it** — GA2.2 was Done for SQLCipher encryption the toolchain cannot do. Done: `applyencryptionkey` and its call in `openstore` are **removed**, replaced by `s.dbencryptionavailable():bool` and `s.dbencryptionstatus():str` in `core.storage.db`, which every assertion about encryption now reads. **Deleting rather than repairing was the decision, and it is the point of the story:** the PRAGMA string was malformed (`PRAGMA key='x''<hex>''`, quotes unbalanced) AND the call discarded its own result on a user-sum error side, so T-18 meant the failure could never surface. Repairing the quoting would have made plain SQLite accept `PRAGMA key`, ignore it, and report success — converting a latent honest failure into a control indistinguishable from real encryption from inside the program, which is exactly the state GA2.2 was marked Done in. `ensuredbkey()` is still called: the key is real and X8.2 will use it for field-level encryption. Three defects, not the two first recorded |
| X8.2 | L | **Done** — 2026-09-27 | **Encrypt the mapping table at rest** — The placeholder↔value mapping is the highest-value data in the system (`docs/threat-model.md:181` rates it Maximum) and is plaintext on disk. SQLCipher is not available and may never be: toke links plain SQLite and there is no sqlcipher anywhere in the toolchain. Use field-level encryption via `std.encrypt` (`aes256gcmencrypt`/`decrypt`/`keygen`/`noncegen`, `hkdfsha` — verified present) with a per-record nonce, applied in `packages/core/src/privacy/placeholder_store.tk`. Do not reinstate a database-level claim.<br><br>**Done 2026-09-27.** Built in `cb5c999` and verified to the evidence standard here. `core.privacy.placeholderstore` seals the whole mapping of one request — value, placeholder and entity type together — as ONE AES-256-GCM payload per request in `placeholder_map_records` (migration 8), padded to 256 bytes, with a fresh 12-byte nonce from `aes256gcmnoncegen` per seal (the sealing function takes no nonce parameter), the request id bound in as AAD, and the key derived by HKDF-SHA256 from the keychain secret. Lookup is by request id, so no value needs to be searchable and there is no blind index or hash of a value anywhere. **Existing plaintext rows are refused, not re-encrypted:** migration 9 drops the old `placeholder_maps` table under `PRAGMA secure_delete`; nothing in the product ever wrote to it. A wrong, missing or unreadable key fails closed — nothing is written, nothing opens, and restoration returns the text unchanged with placeholders intact. Evidence: `tests/unit/privacy/test_mapping_encryption.tk` on the production module — published AES-256-GCM and HKDF known-answer vectors; the round trip; different nonces and ciphertexts for the same payload; wrong key, wrong request and a **deterministic** one-digit flip each refused (the old tamper fixture used the untyped `str.substr` as if it took a length, so it silently truncated the tag and changed nothing in ~60% of runs — fixed, and the test now checks the fixture differs); a byte scan of every file under the data directory (DB, journal, WAL, shm) for each value in plain, hex **and double-hex** form, after a positive control that finds the clear request id. Mutants, each seen red and then restored (`cmp`): (1) seal bypassed but codec kept, both directions — 12 assertions, including the new double-hex scan; (2) a fixed all-zero nonce — 2 (`two seals of the same payload use different nonces`); (3) a default key when the secret is missing — 6 (`storing without a usable key is refused`, `an empty secret derives no key`, …). Smoke: `smoke_e2e.sh` passes under the lock. **Not done:** (a) the live proxy does not persist a mapping at all — `cli/src/proxy.tk`, `cli/src/ask.tk` and `browser/pages/api/pipeline.tk` restore in memory within the request — so the sealed table protects a store nothing in the running product writes today; any future persistence must go through `storemapping`; (b) `test_mapping_deletion.tk` (X8.4) scans for plain text only and PASSED under mutant (1) — its scan should take the hex forms too; (c) the tag check itself is not mutated (that would need a broken `encrypt.c`); the two independent checks in `openpayload` mean removing either one alone is not observable, by design; (d) every other table in `loke.db` stays plaintext (X8.1). |
| X8.3 | M | **Done** — 2026-10-01 | **Keychain-only key handling** — The key is derived through the OS keychain and exists nowhere else: no key file, no environment-variable fallback, no default. A missing key fails the operation rather than falling back to plaintext. Test that removing the keychain entry makes the store unreadable rather than transparently readable.<br><br>**Partial 2026-09-27.** Done: the secret comes from the OS keychain only — service `dev.loke`, account `db_encryption_key`, via `core.storage.keychain` → `std.keychain` (Security.framework at this pin). `core.storage.db.dbkeyfromenv` and the suite's `LOKE_DB_KEY` export are **deleted**, so nothing in the tree reads a key from the environment or a file. `ensuredbkey` no longer overwrites: an item that EXISTS but does not read back as 64 characters now fails the operation (`""`) instead of generating and storing a new key over it, which used to rotate the key on a transient read failure and orphan every sealed row. The decision is `dbkeyaction`, a pure function; `generatedbsecret` is what first use stores. Tests never touch the keychain for this key: the store takes the secret as a parameter. `test_mapping_encryption.tk` asserts all three `dbkeyaction` branches and that, after the entry is removed (the generate branch, a fresh secret), a mapping sealed under the old key does not open and restoration leaves placeholders in place; an empty secret opens nothing. Mutant: the old overwrite behaviour restored in `dbkeyaction` — 2 assertions red (`an item that exists but cannot be read is refused, not overwritten`). **Not done:** (a) `ensuredbkey`'s own keychain calls are exercised by no automated test — a headless process can block on the authorisation dialog, and the suite must not use the login keychain; (b) `std.keychain.exists` is true only on `errSecSuccess`, so a locked or denied keychain reads as "no item" and still takes the generate branch — this needs the OSStatus from toke (upstream ask); (c) nothing in the running product calls `ensuredbkey` (see X8.2 Not done (a)); (d) the suite DOES touch the real login keychain elsewhere — filed as X8.7.<br><br>**Done 2026-10-01.** Closes Not done (a), (b) and (d) above, on toke 3.1.0 (`keychain.lasterrkind`, upstream B4/R4) and X8.7's throwaway keychain. **Built.** `core.storage.db.ensuredbkey` now decides on ONE read: `getdbkey`, then the kind that read left (`core.storage.keychain.lastkind`, new). The `exists()` probe in front of it is gone. `dbkeyaction(kind;value)` replaces `dbkeyaction(present;value)`: 64 characters → use; kind `notfound`, and only that kind, → generate on first use; anything else — `locked`, `denied`, `nokeychain`, `badarg`, `unavailable`, `failed`, an unknown kind, or an item that reads back malformed — → refuse (`""`), never generate. `resolvedbkey()` returns the key with the decision and kind (`$dbkeyresult`); `ensuredbkey()` is its `.key`. **Evidence.** `tests/unit/storage/test_dbkey_keychain.tk` (new) runs the production functions against a throwaway keychain (never the login keychain): `dbkeyaction` over every kind; an absent item → generated, stored, then used unchanged on the next call; a LOCKED keychain holding the key (`security lock-keychain` on the throwaway file) → refused with kind `locked`, and after unlocking the ORIGINAL key is still there; a LOCKED EMPTY keychain → no key returned and none written. `tests/unit/privacy/test_mapping_encryption.tk` updated to the new signature. **Measured, and it changes the story's expected outcome for one case:** a locked file keychain still answers lookups truthfully, so an ABSENT item on it reads `notfound`, not `locked` (toke documents this for `exists`; `get` behaves the same). That is a true "no item", so the first-use branch runs; the store then fails `locked`, the operation gets no key, and the keychain is left empty. Nothing can be orphaned because there is no key, but it is "generate attempted, store failed", not "refused"; the test asserts it as measured. **Mutant:** `dbkeyaction` with `locked` treated as absent → 2 assertions fail (`a LOCKED keychain is refused, never taken as empty`, `a locked keychain holding the key is REFUSED, not taken as empty`); restored, `cmp`-verified. **Not done:** (1) (c) above is unchanged: nothing in the running product calls `ensuredbkey` (X8.2). (2) `denied`, `nokeychain`, `failed` and `unavailable` are asserted through `dbkeyaction` only; no throwaway setup produces them end to end. (3) The authorisation dialog on the user's own login keychain is still untested, because no test may touch that keychain. |
| X8.4 | M | **Done** — 2026-09-27 | **Verifiable deletion** — "Delete everything" is proven by filesystem inspection, not asserted in the interface: after deletion, no file under `~/.loke` contains any mapping value or imported record, verified by a test that greps the tree for known fixture values. Applies to MK21's workspace as well as the mapping table.<br><br>**Done 2026-09-27.** There was no "delete everything" in loke. The nearest things were `core.governance.dsar.processerasure`, which erases one subject's `consent_records` and keeps the audit trail, and `placeholderstore.purgeallmappings`, which empties one table. **Built:** `core.storage.erase.eraseeverything(store)`, a new module, reached from the CLI as `loke erase --everything --yes`. Without `--yes` the command only says what it would remove. It works in two layers. (1) **Database.** It drops EVERY table in `loke.db`, enumerated from `sqlite_master` at run time rather than from a list, so a table added later is erased too. That includes `audit_log`: `DROP` is not blocked by the append-only triggers, and this is the one product path that ends the trail, all of it and never part of it. That is a decision for the user to confirm (see below). The `sqlite_` bookkeeping tables are emptied. The migrations rebuild the schema, so the open store keeps working, and the append-only triggers come back. The file is then `VACUUM`ed with `secure_delete` on, and `PRAGMA freelist_count` must read 0. (2) **Files.** Every other regular file under the data directory is unlinked: the log, `cache/*.vecs` (the semantic cache holds prompts and responses in clear), exports, benchmark results and anything added later. Deletion is the default. Only `loke.db` and its SQLite sidecars (erased in place), `config.toml` and `bin/` are kept. The function refuses a data directory that is not absolute or holds no `loke.db`, and it returns a plain struct (T-18). **Evidence:** `tests/unit/storage/test_erase_everything.tk` runs the production module on a fresh store under `/tmp`, never `~/.loke`. It creates the 20 migrated tables, `dsar_requests` (created the way `core.governance.dsar` creates it), and a table no module names. It writes a row into EVERY table with a per-table fixture in every column, the column list read from `pragma_table_info`. The covered tables include `audit_log`, `disclosure_log` (`fields_disclosed`), `decision_trace`, `nc_artifact_runs`, `approval_requests`, `memory_drawers`, `metrics_raw`, `settings`, `kv` and `placeholder_map_records` (through `storemappingwithsecret`). It also plants the four kinds of file. **Positive controls come first:** each table's fixture and each file's fixture is found before erasure, one value stored only as hex is found by its hex form and not in plain, and one stored only as double hex is found by that form and not as single hex. After erasure, every fixture is searched for in every byte of every file, in plain, hex and double-hex form, and none is found. It makes 123 assertions at this schema (22 tables) and passes. **Mutants**, each seen red and then restored with `cmp`: (a) no `VACUUM`: 2 failures (`no free page remains`, `erased`). The grep alone does not see this one, because `secure_delete` zeroes the pages. (b) `secure_delete` OFF and no `VACUUM`: 9 failures. The fixtures of `approval_requests`, `dsar_requests` and the unnamed table are **found in freed pages**, and so are both encoded-only controls. That is the counterfactual measured on this file. (c) `disclosure_log` skipped: 4 failures, including `no file holds the fixture of disclosure_log`. (d) the file layer skipped: 6 failures, one per planted file. (e) `secure_delete` OFF with `VACUUM` kept: 1 failure, the pragma read-back only. `VACUUM` rewrites every page, so the bytes cannot show it. **The mapping test is widened as the X8.2 worker asked.** `tests/unit/privacy/test_mapping_deletion.tk` now searches plain, hex and double hex, with a hex-only and a double-hex-only control, each shown found by its own form alone. Under X8.2's mutant (seal bypassed, codec kept, both directions), which this test used to PASS, 3 assertions now fail (`BEFORE deletion: the subject's name is already absent … plain, hex or double hex`, and the email and phone). `tests/unit/cli/test_commands.tk` has 7 new parse assertions: only `--everything --yes` erases, and `--no`, a bare `--yes` and trailing arguments are refused. **Smoke:** the real `loke-cli` binary was run with `HOME` set to a throwaway directory. The data seeded with `sqlite3` was found before erasure (plain, hex and in the cache file) and was in no file after it (`grep -a -r`). `freelist_count` read 0, the schema and both triggers were rebuilt, `consent_records` was gone, and `config.toml` and `bin/` were kept. **Defect found and fixed on the way:** `cli.main` matched `cfg.loadconfig`'s `!$lokeerr` result, so under T-18, with no `config.toml`, every config field came from the error payload. `config.datadir` read "could not read or parse …/config.toml", and erase's guard refused it. It now uses the `file.exists` guard from `packages/browser/extensions/core.tk`. `mcp-broker/src/main.tk` has the same shape, filed as X8.8.<br><br>**Not done:** (a) **MK21's workspace does not exist.** MK21 is not built, so there is nothing of it to erase. Any files it writes under the data directory are erased by default, but that is untested. (b) **The user must confirm that `audit_log` should go.** It is destroyed with everything else. `core.governance.dsar` keeps the audit trail for per-subject erasure, and that is unchanged. (c) The erase does not know whether the server is running. The CLI tells the user to stop it, and nothing enforces that. A running server keeps its own connection, and tables its modules create on first use (`consent_records`, `feedback`, …) come back only when used. (d) **Two paths are fixed to `~/.loke`, not the configured data directory:** the log (`shared.log`) and the semantic cache (`page.api.pipeline.cachecfg`). With a non-default `project.data_dir` they are outside what is erased. (e) Unlinked files and the rollback journal SQLite deletes at commit leave their blocks on the volume. APFS is copy-on-write, so overwriting in place would not help either. The claim is about FILES under the data directory, and the physical volume is FileVault's to protect. (f) Per-subject DSAR erasure (`processerasure`) is still not proven by a filesystem test. It runs under the connection's `secure_delete`, but no test reads the bytes. (g) `core.storage.backup.createbackup` has no caller. Backups written outside the data directory would not be erased. |

| X8.11 | S | **Done** — 2026-10-07 | **The headless-Chrome UI checker used a fixed debugging port and left Chrome behind when killed** — Found 2026-10-07 while integrating: two headless Chromes started by `scripts/lib/ui_check.mjs`, 5 and 6 days old, still held `--remote-debugging-port=9333` with their parent gone (init), and two more on 9356 from a worker run. `ui_check.mjs` fixed the port at 9333 (overridable by `UI_CHECK_PORT`) and killed only the browser process in its `finally`, so a gate stopped mid-run (SIGTERM) left Chrome and its helpers running. That plausibly explains this session's intermittent smoke_ui failures ("headless Chrome did not start"; every GA3 check failing at once as if run in another page), seen by W58, W81 and W82; not proven. **Done:** `ui_check.mjs` starts Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and reads the port Chrome chose from `<profile>/DevToolsActivePort`, so concurrent runs and stale Chromes cannot share a port (`UI_CHECK_PORT` still overrides); SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP now kill Chrome and remove the profile. **Evidence:** two runs started concurrently both passed; a run sent SIGTERM after 3 s left no Chrome and no profile; the four orphans were removed by hand (kill -9, by pid). The full gate's smoke_ui exercises it. **Not done:** no automated test of the signal path; Chrome helpers are killed through the browser process only, not by process group. |

the ten orphaned multi-layer modules including `consensus` are **AD1.7**; the audit chain is **GA5.2**
and **GA5.3**.

> and `docs/features-loke.md:161` all record the same blocker: there is no Apple Silicon test machine.
> VM1.4's containerised harness is a partial substitute and cannot validate unified memory or MLX.
> See decision **H** in the open-decisions register.

|-------|------|--------|---------|
| LC1.1 | S | Blocked — hardware | **Acquire or arrange target hardware** — A base Apple Silicon Mac Mini is sufficient and is the recommendation. A cloud GPU instance cannot substitute: unified memory is the premise of the layer-offload design and a discrete-GPU instance has a PCIe boundary that predicts nothing about a Mini; MLX is Apple-Silicon-only, so a non-Apple host validates it not at all. `benchmarks/README.md:42` requires every local-inference figure to state which host produced it. |

Either make it work on the target hardware or remove the MLX claim from the public site and the feature documents. |
| LC1.4 | M | Blocked — LC1.1 | **Validate the CPS 230 continuity control** — `docs/specifications/policy-examples/apra-cps-230.yaml:82,213` carries `validation_status: UNVALIDATED` on the local-provider fallback and states twice that an untested fallback must not be presented to an assessor as a continuity control. This is the control the whole preset rests on. Exercise the degraded path end to end with the network disabled, then change that field and nothing before. |
| LC1.5 | L | Blocked — LC1.1 | **Memory-splitting and layer offload** — Measure what actually fits and at what throughput when a model exceeds available memory, on real unified memory. This is the technique the tiered-inference design assumes; it has never been measured. Report tokens/second and resident memory per tier, and state the physical-security difference between a desk machine and a remote host in any write-up. |

## Epic LS1: Canonical Form Sweep

*toke publishes a measured pattern catalogue and a linter that enforces it. loke has never been run
through either.*

> **Why this is not bikeshedding.** `docs/guide/11-patterns-and-efficiency.md` in the toke repository
> picks one form for each everyday construct **by measurement** — the form that costs the fewest tokens
> under the decision tokenizer *and* runs as fast in as little memory as any alternative. For a project
> whose premise is reducing what is spent on a model, the canonical form is the product, not a style
> preference.
>
> Measured across 223 loke source files on 2026-09-20: **1,668 violations**.
>
> | Rule | Count | Files | Category |
> |---|---|---|---|
> **Re-measured 2026-09-23 over all 535 non-archived `.tk`.** The 2026-09-20 figures below were
> against 223 files and are stale in both directions; LS1.2–LS1.4 must be sized against these.
> The split matters because the trees outside the build cannot be gated until they compile:
>
> | rule | **built set** (`loke`) | repo-wide | category |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `single-use-let` | 854 | **1,823** | hint |
> | `string-concat-chain` | 316 | **814** | warning |
> | `unused-import` | 196 | **306** | warning |
> | **`discarded-value-result`** | **19** | **188** | **error** |
> | `mutable-never-mutated` | 0 | 41 | warning |
> | `unused-let` / `loop-rebuilds-array` / `mut-flag-if` / `flag-soup` | 26 | 58 | mixed |
> | **total** | **1,411** | **3,230** | |
>
> Where the repo-wide error count lives: moke 87, legacy `src/` 79, built set 19, cli 3.
> `src/platform/i18n/locales.tk` alone carries **62** of the 188, in 94 lines — a file nobody has
> ever run. This is why LS1.5's lint gate must be per-tree: a repo-wide error gate would go red the
> instant moke's census is baselined and stay red through the whole onboarding.
>
> **Token efficiency here means canonical constructs, not minified source.** `toke --fmt` is the
> canonical *source* form and makes files slightly larger; `--min` is the shipped form. Do not minify
> source to chase a byte count — the catalogue's verdicts are what count.

| Story | Size | Status | Summary |
|-------|------|--------|---------|
| LS1.1 | S | **Done** — 2026-09-24, built trees at zero | **The 30 `discarded-value-result`, first and on their own** — This is a defect story, not hygiene. The rule is **error** category and its rationale is blunt: *"the discarded value is a bug in every case"*. Arrays and maps have value semantics, so a bare `arr.push(v);` or `trace.steps.push(...)` statement **returns a new collection and throws it away**, and the syntax card notes a bare push *can crash at runtime*. 30 sites in 11 files, worst `agents/observability.tk:222`. The program does not do what it says it does; fix before anything cosmetic.<br><br>**Done 2026-09-24 for the built trees, and the count was wrong in both directions.** This row said 30 `discarded-value-result`. Measured with `toke --lint` across 454 files: **61** sites repo-wide, **10** of them in `packages/core`/`shared`/`browser`. All ten are fixed and the built trees are at **zero**. Every one was a silently empty collection: `installer/pull.tk` ×5 — a model download reported no progress and no outcome whatever happened, and `listinstalledmodels` listed nothing ever; `memory/context.tk` ×4 — L3 deep memory contributed nothing to any context, and `layersloaded` reported `["L0"]` whatever loaded, so that struct's provenance field and its token count disagreed and the half a human reads was the wrong one; `monitoring/sysmon.tk` ×1 — `cleaned.len>4` was always false, so no pid, CPU or RSS was ever read out of `ps`, and the identical defect was found independently in `moke.sysmon.splitws` (two copies of one whitespace splitter, both inert). | LS1.1a | L | **Done** | **Thirteen accumulations that silently do nothing** — The most consequential defect found in the whole migration, and **no lint rule reports it**. ## Epic RV1: Re-verify the Done Markers That Need a Binary

*The build was red for four months. Roughly 120 stories were marked Done by reading code.*

> **The problem, stated plainly.** A story marked Done for behaviour that has never executed is worse
> than one marked not-started: it is an assertion with no evidence, and this document is the input to
> `claims.md`, which is the input to everything the project says publicly. Two examples already found and
> corrected show the shape — the X4a.6 preamble asserted *"All 172 modules compile, 19/19 tests pass"*
> when 58 of 199 compiled, and GA2.2 was Done for SQLCipher encryption the toolchain cannot do at all.
>
> Every row in scope gets exactly one of three outcomes. **Holds** — exercised and true, with the
> command that showed it. **Reopened** — exercised and false. **Untestable** — names what is missing.
> "Done" without one of those three is not an acceptable result for any row here.
>
> **Amended 2026-09-23, after the first pass at RV1.4 found markers wrong in BOTH directions.**
> Three Done rows are false — **GA1.2**, **GA1.4**, **GA1.8**, each now Reopened with the code that
> disproves it. One open row is done — **LS1.1a**, 11 of 13 landed. So a ledger that can only reopen is
> not a reconciliation, and RV1.1a is added for the inverse direction.
>
> Two further amendments the first pass forced:
>
> - **RV1.1 is not 65 rows of equal weight.** Only 26 of 122 test files import a production module,
>   reaching 21 distinct ones. Every T1–T14 row whose subject is outside those 21 is unverifiable *by
>   construction* — the verdict is "untestable", takes a minute, and needs no code reading. Partition
>   before working it, or RV1.1 reads as 65 code reviews when most of it is a join.
> - **X7 is the method, RV1 is the ledger, and the unit of work is one story row — not one test file.**
>   De-stubbing `tests/unit/privacy/test_placeholder.tk` *is* how GA1.2 gets re-verified. Scheduling
>   X7.2 and RV1.4 apart means reading the same module twice and writing two verdicts that can disagree.
>
> **RV1.7 could not start with counts, because the table schema was broken. RV1.7a fixed it
> 2026-09-23.** Recorded so the shape is not reintroduced: splitting story rows on `|` gave 551 rows
> with 6 fields, **38 with 5** — G1.1–G4.6 and AG1.1–AG1.8 used a 3-column table with **no status
> column at all**, carrying status as a trailing `**[Done]**` inside the description — and 5 with 7 or
> 8, read as unescaped `|` inside a cell. Status values were inconsistent in form too: 347 `**Done**`,
> 72 bare `Done`, 82 blank, plus `Blocked — …`, `Queued behind …`, `**Reopened**` and free prose. That
> is why two careful parses of this file disagreed on its own row count (598/477 against 594/485).
>
> The repair also corrected that survey. The 3-column tables were eight, not five — M1, M2 and X5 as
> well as G1–G4 and AG1, 40 rows — and only one row, AG1.7, had genuinely unescaped `|`; the other four
> were already written `\|` and it was the splitter that was wrong. Four rows had no closing `|` at all
> (F10.7, F10.11, RS1, RS2), which GFM renders anyway. The schema is now gated by
> [`scripts/check_backlog.py`](../scripts/check_backlog.py) (RV1.7b), and the counts in **SUMMARY** are
> generated from the rows.

The same inverse sweep closed nine F10 rows on 2026-09-23 (F10.23a–g, F10.12a, F10.30), which were open only because nobody had marked them. Finding more cases like this is ongoing RV1 work and is not tracked under this row. |
| RV1.7a | S | **Done** — 2026-09-23 | **Repair the table schema before anything is derived from it** — Every story row gets exactly 4 columns; the 38 rows in G1–G4 and AG1 gain a real status column instead of a `**[Done]**` buried in the description; no unescaped `\|` inside a cell; and status is drawn from a closed set — blank, `Spec done`, `Done`, `Reopened`, `⏸ On hold — <reason>`, `Blocked — <ID>`, `Queued behind <ID>`, `Partial — <reason>`. Rationale belongs in the description, not the status cell. **Nothing downstream is derivable until this holds**, which is why it is split out of RV1.7<br><br>**Status detail — done 2026-09-23.** All 629 story rows now carry four cells and a closing `\|`. F10.7, F10.11, RS1 and RS2 had no closing `\|` at all. 47 status cells held rationale too long for the column; every one was moved verbatim into the Summary after `**Status detail:**`, and the transformation was checked to lose no word. `Spec done` is removed from the legend rather than kept on zero rows, and `Superseded by <ID>` is added because one row needed it. |

### RV1.1 worked, 2026-09-23 — the partition, and why it is a join rather than 65 code reviews

The epic preamble demands runtime evidence. **Sixty-five** rows carry a file path in their own
description, so the first question about each is not "is this behaviour correct" but "does the file
this row cites exist, and does it exercise anything". That is a join against the tree, and it
settles fifty-one of the sixty-five without reading any production code.

One mechanical criterion per bucket, applied uniformly to all 65 so the sweep is auditable and
reversible:

| Bucket | Criterion | Rows | Verdict |
|---|---|--:|---|
| **A** | the named file is **not in the live tree** — it is in `_archived-tests/`, which `scripts/run_tests.sh` excludes by an explicit `-not -path '*/_archived-tests/*'` | **37** | **untestable** — no run has ever exercised it, in CI or locally |
| **B** | the named file exists and passes, and imports nothing but `std.*` — it declares its subject inside the test file | **0** | **untestable** — it cannot fail when the module changes |
| **C** | the named file exists and imports production code — so it was compiled, linked and run | **28** | **holds** (24) or **reopened** (4) |

Bucket A is the sharpest single fact in this reconciliation: **37 of the 65 Done markers cite a test
file that no runner can see.** Not a file that fails, not a file that was weakened — a file the
discovery glob removes before compilation. T8.1–T8.10 name `tests/unit/platform/*`, T10.1–T10.5 name
`tests/unit/governance_src/*`, T11.1–T11.4 name `tests/unit/mcp_broker/*` and
`tests/unit/memory_src/*`, T12.1–T12.3 name `tests/unit/feedback/*` and `tests/unit/agents/…`, and
T14.1 and T14.3 name integration and e2e files that were archived with them. Each is now
**Reopened** — and the reason is stated on the row itself, because "Reopened" without it would read
as an assertion having been disproved, which is not what happened. What is missing is the test, and
it is named.

Bucket B started the day at 26 and **ended at zero**, because X7.2 was worked at the same time and on
the same files — which is the reason the two epics are one piece of work. De-stubbing
`tests/unit/privacy/test_placeholder.tk` **is** how T1.2 gets re-verified; scheduling them apart
would mean reading the same module twice and writing two verdicts that can disagree. Every row whose
named file is in the live tree now cites a test that imports the module it is about, so bucket C is
the whole of the answerable set.

Bucket C is where the value is, and it is where both directions appear. Twenty-four rows **hold**, each
with the command that showed it written on the row. Four are **reopened on a failing assertion against
real code**, not on paperwork:

| Row | Test | What is false |
|---|---|---|
| **T2.5** | `tests/unit/router/test_intent.tk` | intent classification always answers `chat` with `method:"llm"` and confidence 0.72, whatever the prompt, because all three of its stdlib-result matches are error-arm-first. `router.tk:308` feeds that task into model selection on every request |
| **T3.3** | `tests/unit/optimiser/test_toon.tk` | `measuresavings` returns a bare `f64` across a module boundary and is corrupted (T-20) — the returned values are denormals whose bit patterns are `str.len` of the second argument |
| **T5.1** | `tests/unit/storage/test_settings.tk` | all four setters bind `"now()"` as a parameter, so `updated_at` stores the seven characters `n-o-w-(-)` |
| **T6.3** | `tests/unit/memory/test_decay.tk` | five assertions against `core.memory.decay`, including `apply` returning `-inf` at every age — and `sweeprows` deletes below a floor |

A fifth would have been `tests/unit/governance/test_scorecard.tk`: its `countquery` defect was measured
and reported, another worker fixed it in source during the same session, and the test is green against
the repair. It is named here because it is the clearest single demonstration of the epic's value.

**The moke and CLI rows are untestable for two different reasons, and the difference matters.**
`packages/moke/` fails to compile — 52 `COMPILE_FAIL` lines over 42 source files in
`build/trees/moke/break-report.txt`, including every module moke's 33 tests are named after. The CLI
tree, by contrast, builds **clean** (zero `COMPILE_FAIL`) and is invisible only because
`scripts/run_tests.sh` passes a single `-I build/interfaces` and links `packages/browser/build/ooke`
alone; a hand-built probe against `build/trees/loke-cli/interfaces` links and runs `cli.commands`
successfully. One is a code problem, the other is a one-line runner change. See
[test-coverage.md](test-coverage.md) for both measurements.
